title: Parse a Date String of Unknown Format
statement:
You receive date strings of exactly **10 characters** whose format and separators are not fixed. Each string looks like `yyyy_mm_dd`, `mm/dd/yyyy`, `2024__2__9`, and so on. Your job is to detect the separators, extract the three components and print the date in a standard form.

Every string satisfies these guarantees:

- It starts and ends with a digit and contains exactly three maximal runs of digits (the **fields**). Between consecutive fields is a **separator**: a run of one or more non-digit, non-whitespace characters (any such character is allowed, the two separators may differ in length and in characters, and a separator can be longer than one character).
- Exactly one of the first and last fields has exactly 4 digits: it is the **year**. The other two fields have 1 or 2 digits each (a leading zero is allowed).

How to read the fields:

- If the year is the **first** field, the order is year, month, day.
- If the year is the **last** field, the order is **month, day**, year (so `03/04/2024` is the 4th of March, never the 3rd of April).

Then validate the date with the Gregorian calendar: the year must be at least `1`, the month between `1` and `12`, and the day must exist in that month (February has 29 days in a leap year: a year divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100 that are not divisible by 400).

For each input string print the date as `YYYY-MM-DD` (zero-padded), or `INVALID` if the date is not a real calendar date.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `q`, the number of strings.
Each of the next `q` lines contains one 10-character string.
output_format: Print `q` lines: for each string, the normalized `YYYY-MM-DD` date or `INVALID`.
constraints: Every string has length exactly 10 and follows the guarantees above

examples.explanation: The first string has the year first: 2024, 03, 15. In the second the year is last, so the order is month 03, day 15, year 2024. In the third the separators are two underscores each, and the fields 2024, 2 and 9 give 2024-02-09.

02/30/2023 has no 30th of February. 2024 is a leap year, so 2024.02.29 is valid, while 2023.02.29 is not. In 13--1-2020 the year is last, so the month is 13 even though 13 could have been a day: invalid.

hints: Do not try to guess the separator character. Scan the string and collect the maximal runs of digits; anything that is not a digit is a separator.
The year is the field with 4 digits. Check whether it is the first or the last field to decide whether the order is year-month-day or month-day-year.
Validation is separate from parsing: check the month range, then compare the day with the days in that month, adjusting February for leap years. Print with zero padding.
